inventory.notes: White masthead with a small bin glyph and 'Dunmore District Council' in bold body sans; nav 'Book a slot', 'Opening days'. Pale grey-green ground. Eye goes 1) 'Book a slot' H1, 2) the row of seven amber 'Few left' tags (the only warm colour on the page), 3) the day chips. Primary action 'Next' (filled dark green) sits below the full grid. Slots: an unlabelled first row of 'Few left' slots, then 'Morning' and 'Afternoon' groups; full slots greyed with a 'Full' tag. Opening days in a bordered white box. One sans family, bold for headings. 4px corners, borders, no shadows, no imagery. Copy: 'Choose a day and the 20-minute slot you will arrive in; the gate checks the reference and the vehicle.' No memorable element. Dark theme composed with lighter greens on dark green-grey; equally bare.

'Back to the slots' link directly above the H1 with no gap. Segmented vehicle buttons (Car, Car with trailer, Van) plus an (i) button that opens an inline permit explanation. Permit field, then seven bordered checkbox rows for waste. Eye: H1, vehicle buttons, the column of checkbox rows. Errors: red-bordered summary 'There is a problem' with linked messages, inline red messages. At 1280 the form occupies the left ~610px; the right half is empty. Copy firm and concrete: 'Rubble is limited to four bags and mattresses to two.'

'Your booking' summary card (Day, Slot, Vehicle, Waste with Change links), then four labelled inputs, a line 'Nothing is paid. Bring the reference and something with your address on it.', and 'Book this slot'. Expired state: red-bordered 'There is a problem / This slot is no longer available.' above the summary, slot row reads '– · Change slot', and 'Book this slot' remains the primary button.

H1 'Booked'; full-width card 'Your reference' with DR-204117 at ~32px bold; 'At the centre' card; outlined 'Book another slot'. No day, time or vehicle shown. At 1280 the reference card stretches full width with content in the left half, the second card stops at half width, and a grey band remains under the footer. Cancelled state keeps H1 'Booked' and the reminder sentence, adding a red line 'Status: cancelled. This booking is not on the gate's list.'

inventory.not_assessable: Feedback, focus rings, hover, the 120ms fades and screen-reader behaviour cannot be judged from stills.

swap.evidence: Swapped products: a GP surgery appointment booker and a library study-room booker. Surviving unchanged: the masthead (name in body sans + small icon), the green-on-pale palette, outlined day chips, the boxed time grid with availability tags, bordered summary card, form inputs, reference card. Bound to this product: only content (vehicle/permit/waste choices, '20-minute slot', 'Show this at the gate'). With the name and copy hidden, a reader could not tell it is for a recycling centre.

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a council booking service: light ground, one sober green or navy accent, GOV.UK-like bold sans headings, outlined option buttons, red-bordered error summary, bordered summary list, phone number in a footer. Predicted opposite: a friendly rounded consumer-app look with illustration. The design matches the default on type voice, colour anchor, shape and every component.

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'booking for a council sports hall's badminton courts, for residents on phones'. Predicted: day chips, a grid of time buttons with 'Few left'/'Full' tags, a step indicator, a summary card with Change links, a reference card at the end, Restrained green. Overlap is near-total; nothing in the visual layer was driven by the tip, its gate, its bays or the van-permit rule.

evidence: All three tests fail on the identity-carrying elements (masthead, colour anchor, type voice, slot grid, done card).
Product-specific only through copy and the vehicle/waste content; no signature from the product's world.
Conventional Operate structure is correct and not counted against it; the gap is the brand layer, which is a category default.

unfinished: identity is only the council name set in bold body sans with a generic bin glyph; no designed mark for the recycling centre
no focal point or signature on any screen; every surface is heading + controls + bordered box

done page at 1280: reference card spans full width with text in the left half only, the 'At the centre' card stops at half width, and an empty grey band sits under the footer (done/default/1280-light)
vehicle page at 1280: single ~610px form column with the right half of the canvas empty (vehicle/van/1280-light)
headings differ from body only in size and weight within the same family; no typographic moment
'Back to the slots' link butts directly against the H1 with no space (vehicle/*/1280-light, 375-light)
slot grids end in ragged single-item rows (16:40 and 17:20 alone at 375, root/slot-chosen/375-light)
evidence: Clean and orderly with a tidy green primary button and readable type, but a first-time resident sees a default form: no imagery of the centre, no colour doing work beyond the button and the amber 'Few left' tags.
Nothing on the done page makes the reference feel like the ticket to show at the gate: DR-204117 is a medium-size heading in a plain white box (done/default/375-light).
Dark theme is composed competently (root/default/1280-dark) but equally bare.

attributes.x_evidence: Council name in the masthead; plain sentence-case labels; address, postcode and phone in the footer; 'Nothing is paid.'; no marketing language, no hero, no stock imagery.
Plain copy and one filled button per step; rules beside controls.
attributes.y_evidence: Bare: no mark, no imagery, no signature; done page is two bordered boxes with half-empty space at 1280; vehicle page leaves half the canvas empty; headings are body text in bold. The reference, the one thing residents carry to the gate, gets no treatment beyond a heading size.

attributes.pair: firm about the rules, not stern
attributes.x_evidence: 'Rubble is limited to four bags and mattresses to two.', 'Starts DRC-, then five digits.', inline permit explanation 'A van, or a car with a trailer, needs a free permit... comes by email within two working days.', 'Bring the reference and something with your address on it.'
attributes.y_evidence: Errors use red-bordered summary and red inline text but wording stays neutral ('Choose the vehicle you are bringing.'). Not stern.

mode_fit: All four surfaces are Operate/Read and stay quiet and conventional in structure, which is right; no hero moments or choreography. The issue is not too much expression but no identity floor (brand-expression §3.5: identity is not a hero moment).

specificity.label: (judged)
specificity.evidence: Anchor 1: product content (vehicle/waste choices, gate copy, DR- reference) sits on a frame that fails the swap, category-guess and similar-prompt tests.

hierarchy.label: (judged)
hierarchy.evidence: Anchor 3: on every step H1, the controls and the single filled button read in order and survive a squint. Named lapse: on 'when' the amber 'Few left' row is the loudest element and sits above the Morning/Afternoon groups, competing with the day choice and pulling slots out of time order (root/default/1280-light).

coherence.label: (judged)
coherence.evidence: Anchor 3: one type family, one green, 4px radius, borders throughout, dark theme composed rather than inverted. Minor lapse: the cancelled done state keeps the 'Booked' heading and reminder copy of the success state.

restraint.label: (judged)
restraint.evidence: Capped at 2: no focal point and no signature anywhere; nothing decorative to remove, but restraint has left emptiness, not a decision (DSL-080).

brand_fit.label: (judged)
brand_fit.evidence: Two of three pairs reflected; 'plain, not bare' slides to bare on every surface (see brand_fit).

execution.label: (judged)
execution.evidence: Anchor 2: clean at the main phone width; rough at the edges: done page at 1280 with half-width second card and a grey band under the footer; 'Back to the slots' jammed against the H1; ragged single-slot rows; cancelled state copy contradicts itself; expired state still leads with 'Book this slot'.

appeal.label: (judged)
appeal.evidence: Anchor 2, matches verdict 'plain': clean but the identity is only the name; nothing on any screen rewards a look.

critic_only: Done page omits day, time and vehicle
'Few left' slots removed from the Morning/Afternoon groups into an unlabelled row
Bare identity / no signature (brand pair 'plain, not bare')
Done page wide-layout gaps; back link spacing
detector_comparison.post_unseal_notes: Zero detector hits is consistent with my reading: the page is tell-free and clean, which is exactly why the gap is appeal and specificity rather than measurable tells. No change to verdicts.

findings.title: Cancelled booking still headed 'Booked' and promises a reminder
findings.description: In the cancelled state of the done page the H1 still reads 'Booked' and the card still says 'Show this at the gate' and 'A reminder will be sent to your mobile the evening before.' The only sign of cancellation is one red line, 'Status: cancelled. This booking is not on the gate's list.', set at body size under the reference.
findings.impact: The page's loudest signals (H1, reference, gate instructions) say the booking stands; the cancellation is tertiary.

harm.statement: A resident glancing at the done page on a phone may read 'Booked' and the reference, drive to Quarry Road with a loaded car, and be turned away at the gate because the booking is not on the list.

locations.snippet: Booked / Status: cancelled. This booking is not on the gate's list. / A reminder will be sent...

evidence.detail: H1 'Booked' at top; red status line inside reference card

findings.recommendation: Decide what the cancelled state's headline and first line must say so that the cancellation outranks the reference, and drop success-only copy from that state.

findings.title: Done page does not show the day, slot time or vehicle booked
findings.description: The done page shows only the reference DR-204117, gate instructions and a 'Book another slot' button. The day (Saturday 17 October), the 09:20-09:40 slot and the vehicle, all shown on the confirm page, are absent.
findings.impact: The surface's job in PRODUCT.md is 'know the booking is made and what to show at the gate'; the gate checks the vehicle against the booking and a slot holds a 20-minute window.

harm.statement: A resident who reopens this page the next morning, or prints it, cannot see which day and 20-minute slot they booked or which vehicle it is for, so they may arrive outside their slot or with the wrong vehicle and be turned away.

evidence.detail: No date, time or vehicle anywhere on the page
Confirm page shows Day, Slot, Vehicle which the done page drops

findings.recommendation: Decide which booking facts the gate and the resident need beside the reference, and present them as one unit that reads from a phone held up at the gate.

findings.title: 'Few left' slots are pulled out of the Morning/Afternoon groups into an unlabelled row
findings.description: On the 'when' step, slots with few places left appear in a separate first row with no heading (08:20, 09:20, 12:00, 12:20, 12:40, 13:40, 14:20 on Monday; at 375 ten slots on Saturday). They are missing from the chronological 'Morning' and 'Afternoon' lists that follow, which therefore skip times (Morning goes 08:00, 08:40, 09:00, 09:40...). The amber row is also the loudest element on the page.
findings.impact: Residents think in times ('Saturday morning'); the grid splits time order by availability without saying so.

harm.statement: A resident scanning 'Morning' for 09:20 does not find it there and may conclude it is gone, or must cross-check two lists, slowing the choice of slot on a phone.

evidence.detail: unlabelled 'Few left' row above 'Morning'; 08:20 and 09:20 absent from Morning

findings.recommendation: Decide whether scarcity is a property of a slot shown in place or a separate group; if separate, it needs a heading and the time lists must stay complete.

findings.title: No identity or signature: 'plain' has become 'bare'
findings.description: Across all four steps the only identity is 'Dunmore District Council' in bold body sans with a small bin glyph. No element comes from the centre's world (the gate, the bays, the permit, the reference read at the gate). DESIGN.md declares 'plain, not bare'.
findings.impact: Design note: the service reads as a default form and the brand pair's Y side is what shows.
findings.recommendation: Choose one element from the centre's own mechanism (most naturally the reference shown at the gate) and give it a treatment that carries 'plain, not bare' on every step.

findings.title: Done page at wide widths: stretched card, half-width card, band under footer
findings.description: At 1280 the reference card spans the full content width with its text in the left half, the 'At the centre' card stops at half width, and the page ends with an empty grey band below the white footer.
findings.impact: Design note: the final screen looks unfinished on desktop.
findings.recommendation: Decide one measure for the done page's content and apply it to both cards; let the footer meet the bottom of short pages.

findings.title: 'Back to the slots' link sits flush against the H1
findings.description: On the vehicle step the back link has no space between it and 'Your vehicle and waste', so the two read as one block.
findings.impact: Design note: spacing rhythm breaks at the top of the step.
findings.recommendation: Apply the spacing scale between the back link and the heading.

findings.title: Expired-slot state keeps 'Book this slot' as the primary action
findings.description: When the held slot has expired, the error says 'This slot is no longer available.', the slot row shows '–', yet the filled 'Book this slot' button remains the only primary action; the route back is a small 'Change slot' link in the summary.
findings.impact: Design note: the strongest element on the page asks for an action that cannot succeed.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the primary action is when the hold has lapsed and let the error lead to it.

strengths: Rules stated beside the control they govern (rubble and mattress limits, permit format, inline permit explanation) - carries 'firm, not stern'.
One filled button per step and a dark theme composed with its own greens, not inverted.
Error summary with linked messages plus inline messages, consistent across steps.
keep: Keep the gate-attendant voice and the rule-beside-the-control pattern; any added identity must not dilute them.
